item.title: Indonesia teen with ‘Superman’ cape fights haze fires, minister hails ‘forest hero’
item.description: Dressed as his favourite superhero, Indonesian teenager Rudiyansah walks along a charred landscape, helping douse wildfires that have razed large parts of Borneo island. The Southeast Asian country has been battling infernos that have left a thick, blanketing smog over parts of the island that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei. Rudiyansah’s red and blue Superman costume stood out against the stark, scorched landscape surrounding the town of Palangkaraya, where he has joined a local... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: Venezuela: Two months after the quake, 12,500 people still live in temporary camps
item.description: Two months after two earthquakes struck Venezuela, more than 12,500 people are still living in temporary camps in La Guaira. Many survivors are still struggling to come to terms with the loss of loved ones and their homes. They have been forced to adapt to precarious living conditions, exposed to the elements, with little access to medical care and humanitarian aid. France 24 reporters Herminia Fernández and Julio Uribarris visited three camps housing earthquake survivors. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: How Texas turned an abandoned golf course into five lakes to control flood
item.description: Exploration Green in Clear Lake City, Texas, transformed a former golf course into a 200-acre green space with stormwater detention lakes, wetlands and recreation areas. The project was created to help reduce flooding in the community, with its five planned detention lakes capable of storing 500 million gallons of water. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Tech paradox: fear of being left behind drives China non-programmers to build own AI tools
item.description: A growing number of non-programmers across China are developing their own AI tools, primarily motivated by concerns about falling behind as technology reshapes work and daily life. The anxiety surrounding this shift is almost palpable. AI courses and side-hustle tutorials have flooded mainland social media as employers increasingly expect their workers to develop AI literacy. item.title: Panama Canal to reduce shipping over El Nino-fuelled drought
item.description: The Panama Canal will cut the number of ships passing through it starting next month because of drought caused by the El Nino phenomenon, the operator of the strategic waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific said on Thursday. From September 3, the number of vessels allowed through each day will fall from 36 to 34 due to low water levels in two artificial lakes that feed the canal, the Panama Canal Authority said. item.title: En 1998, Honduras construyó un puente a prueba de huracanes. Soportó el Mitch, pero quedó inutilizado: el río cambió de cauce
item.description: En Honduras, en la ciudad de Choluteca, hay un puente con una historia curiosa. Un poco más allá del puente de Choluteca o puente Carías está el que nos interesa: el Nuevo Puente de Choluteca o Puente Sol Naciente , construido a finales de los 90 para descongestionar el tráfico que entraba a la ciudad por el puente original. Su nombre tan japonés no es casualidad: de allí procede el dinero para su construcción y la empresa constructora que lo puso en pie . Como curiosidad, es el puente más largo de Honduras y por allí pasa la gran carretera Panamericana . Como curiosidad también, hubo un… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: This US island was set to become a resort until 2 storms changed everything
item.description: Assateague Island was once planned as a major resort community with thousands of homes, roads and commercial areas. Two powerful storms changed that future. A 1933 hurricane split the island, while the 1962 Ash Wednesday storm destroyed roads and structures. The island was later protected as a National Seashore in 1965, preserving its beaches, wildlife and natural coastal habitats. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Jharkhand's Dhanbad turned a barren coal-belt hillock green; CISF is now trying the same experiment on 6 acres along Delhi’s Yamuna
item.description: In a remarkable effort to rejuvenate Delhi's Yamuna floodplain, CISF personnel have embarked on an ambitious forest reclamation project. By planting thousands of trees and vetiver grass near Sarai Kale Khan, they aim to combat land degradation and curb soil erosion along the riverbank. This initiative, inspired by a successful ecological effort in Dhanbad's mining regions, is part of a larger strategy for restoring and preserving the Yamuna floodplain. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.description: Beach patrols report hundreds of stings a day as warmer waters and drought create favorable conditions for jellyfish An unusually high number of jellyfish are crowding Delaware’s beaches this summer amid climate change and other environmental factors – keeping some beachgoers out of the ocean and stinging lifeguards as well as bathers. Beach safety patrols in the state have reported hundreds of daily stings as the jellyfish have increased with intensifying environmental factors, including warmer waters, hot and dry conditions, and water circulation favorable to the invertebrates. item.title: France's Fontainebleau forest reopens one month after wilfire
item.description: Good news for hiking and climbing enthusiasts today: the Fontainebleau Forest just South of Paris is set to reopen to the public. Portions of the forest remain closed to the public. Story by France 2 and Camille Corcoran. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: New snake species named after Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash; here’s why scientists chose him
item.description: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have unveiled a new non-venomous snake species from New Guinea, named Lielaphis slashi. This remarkable naming pays tribute to Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, also known as Saul Hudson, who has always been captivated by reptiles and the natural world. First encountered during past fieldwork, this small ground-dwelling snake signifies the incredible biodiversity and urgent conservation efforts needed in New Guinea.
